title: QUIC quic-go Client Download-Liveness Completion Boundary Architecture
purpose: Describe the bounded completion contract that keeps the quic-go client transfer/keyupdate drain path visible as the remaining local candidate while completing downloads against the known mounted source-length body and leaving msquic TLS-alert-50 cells outside the candidate set.
design_summary: The existing peer-characterization surface already shows that the remaining Incursa-side candidate is the quic-go client transfer/keyupdate drain path. This architecture formalizes that candidate as a trace-first slice, preserves the msquic TLS-alert-50 cells as peer-side noise, and keeps the work bounded to download completion on the mounted source-length body. It does not widen into a generic keepalive policy or broader server-role behavior.
alternatives_considered: Jump directly to a runtime keepalive implementation. Rejected because the current request is to formalize the slice first, not to change transport behavior before the proof boundary is stable.

Reclassify the msquic TLS-alert-50 cells as a local Incursa bug. Rejected because the preserved major-peer evidence still looks peer-side and the current slice should not overstate local responsibility.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The quic-go candidate must remain bounded to client transfer and keyupdate drain behavior.
Peer-specific TLS-alert-50 cells must remain distinguishable from the local candidate set.
The slice must stay bounded to the known mounted source-length completion boundary and must not be read as a generic keepalive policy.
No server-role or public API widening should be introduced as part of this formalization.
data_and_state_considerations: The slice reads repo-local status and gap notes plus the preserved major-peer evidence narrative. The completion helper can be verified locally without a new runner bundle, while the major-peer evidence remains the motivation for the boundary.
risks: Readers may overread the slice as a generic keepalive policy if the source-length boundary is not kept explicit.
The quic-go drain candidate could drift into broader runtime work before the bounded download completion contract is verified.

supplemental_sections.heading: Scope
supplemental_sections.content: This design only formalizes the bounded download completion candidate. It does not promote support for msquic or widen the major-peer matrix profile.
